beats.title: A conversation and your history
beats.copy: We'll talk through what's going on, how it started, what makes it better or worse, and what you want to get back to.

beats.title: A physical assessment
beats.copy: We'll look at how you move, test strength and range of movement, and work out what's likely driving your symptoms.

beats.title: Treatment usually starts the same visit
beats.copy: Most people leave their first appointment having already had some hands-on treatment, not just an assessment.

beats.title: A plain-English plan to take away
beats.copy: We'll explain what we think is going on, how long it's likely to take, and set you up with a home exercise plan.

whatToWear.suggestion: Shorts, or trousers that roll up above the knee
A vest top, or something with straps we can move aside
Comfortable, loose-fitting clothing you can move freely in
Flat, comfortable shoes if we're assessing your walking or running

whatToBring: A timeline of when your symptoms started and what's changed since
Any GP letters, referral letters or clinic correspondence about this problem
Scan or X-ray results, if you've had any
A list of any medication you're currently taking
Your insurance details, if you're claiming through a health insurer

steps.title: Book directly
steps.copy: Call or book online — no referral or authorisation needed. You pay for each session as you go.

steps.title: Pay after your visit
steps.copy: We take payment by card at the end of each appointment; a receipt is available if you'd like to claim it back yourself.

steps.title: Check your policy first
steps.copy: Call your insurer before booking to confirm physiotherapy is covered and get an authorisation reference.

steps.title: Give us your details
steps.copy: Bring your policy number, authorisation reference and insurer's claims-line number to your first visit.

steps.title: We invoice your insurer where we can
steps.copy: Where your insurer allows direct billing we invoice them for you; otherwise you pay us and reclaim the cost yourself.

insured.preAuthCopy: Most insurers ask you to call them for a pre-authorisation reference before your first session — without it, they may decline the claim. We're happy to give you anything we can to help that call.
insured.excessCopy: Many policies carry an excess — an amount you pay yourself before your insurer contributes. Check your policy documents or call your insurer to confirm yours.
insured.gpReferralCopy: Some insurers need a GP referral letter before they'll approve physiotherapy; others accept self-referral. This varies by insurer and policy, so it's worth checking before you book.
